title: Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Forecasting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (Playbook 2033)
author: Elena Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standardized processes and templates for annual budgeting, rolling forecasting, procurement approvals, contract lifecycle management, and revenue recognition & billing treatment. It is intended for finance partners, business unit leads, procurement, legal, and owners of cost centers. Use this document as the single source of truth for policy, thresholds, and step-by-step procedures for FY planning and day-to-day transactions.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood entities and product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize).
- Covers annual budget submissions, monthly rolling forecasts, capital and expense procurement, standard contract workflow, and revenue recognition/billing policy for subscription, usage-based, and professional services revenue.

Key definitions

- Budget: The approved annual financial plan used for targets and headcount/cost commitments.
- Forecast: A rolling 12-month projection updated monthly to reflect actuals and near-term expectations.
- CapEx: Capital expenditures (hardware, on-prem packaging, non-cloud capitalized costs).
- OpEx: Operating expenditures (SaaS, cloud, software, headcount).
- ARR: Annual Recurring Revenue.
- RevRec: Revenue recognition in accordance with ASC 606 principles.

Roles & ownership

- Finance (FP&A): Lead owner for budgeting and forecasting process, consolidation, variance analysis, and model maintenance.
- Business Unit (BU) Leads / Product Managers: Submit budget requests, provide forecasts, and own variance explanations.
- People Ops: Provide headcount plans and hiring cadence input.
- Procurement: Approve and execute non-standard purchasing, maintain preferred vendor list.
- Legal: Review and sign contracts, manage exceptions and non-standard terms.
- Finance-legal team: Policy owner and final approver for revenue recognition interpretations.

Budgeting process (annual)

1. Timeline
   - Aug–Sep: Budget templates & guidance published by FP&A.
   - Oct: BU planning workshops and draft submissions due.
   - Nov: Consolidation, scenario modeling, and executive reviews.
   - Dec: Final budget approval and board submission.

2. Templates & inputs
   - Use the centralized budgeting workbook (Finance Drive / Budgeting 2033). Required inputs: headcount plan, cloud spend by service, capital requests, new initiatives (RACI, milestones, expected KPIs).

3. Approval thresholds
   - Up to $25k: BU lead approval.
   - $25k–$250k: Procurement + Finance approval.
   - > $250k: Executive sponsor + Finance Director sign-off; if multi-year, require Legal & CFO review.

4. Capital requests
   - Provide business case, expected useful life, depreciation method, and tagging. Hardware purchases intended for Dedicated/Private offerings must be marked as CapEx.

Forecasting cadence (rolling 12-month)

- Frequency: Monthly updates (due first business day of month for prior month actuals + 12-month forward view).
- Drivers: Bookings, usage trends (tokens/embedding units), churn, pricing changes, major deals, hiring schedule, and fleet capacity events.
- Confidence buckets: High (validated deals), Medium (probability-weighted pipeline), Low (early-stage opportunities).
- Variance reporting: >5% variance to budget or prior forecast in ARR or spend requires a variance memo with remediation plan.

Procurement procedures

1. Purchase categorization
   - Standard: Subscriptions, approved SaaS, routine hardware replacement. Managed by Procurement catalog for auto-approval up to $25k.
   - Non-standard / Strategic: New vendors, professional services, or contracts with indemnities; requires Procurement + Legal review.

2. Request flow (step-by-step)
   1. Submit purchase requisition in Procurement Portal with cost center and GL code. Attach SOW/quote.
   2. Procurement validates vendor, checks preferred vendor status, and runs vendor risk questionnaire if new.
   3. Finance verifies budget availability.
   4. Approvals routed automatically based on thresholds above.
   5. Purchase order (PO) issued for approved requests.

3. Emergency/Budget-exempt purchases
   - For urgent operational needs (incident remediation, security), Procurement will issue expedited review; Finance to retrospectively approve within 5 business days. Document rationale and owner.

4. Vendor onboarding & payments
   - KYC and tax forms required for new vendors. Procurement registers vendor in ERP. Payment terms default to Net 30 unless negotiated.

Contract lifecycle management

1. Standard contract types
   - Master Services Agreement (MSA), Statement of Work (SOW), Software License, NDA, Reseller/Partner Agreement.

2. Review & signature flow
   1. Initiator selects template from Contract Library.
   2. Legal performs risk review and marks non-standard clauses.
   3. Procurement verifies commercial terms (pricing, SLAs, payment terms).
   4. Finance assesses revenue & accounting impacts (upfront payments, deferred revenue).
   5. Authorized signatory executes contract.

3. Contract exceptions & escalation
   - Any change to liability caps, indemnities, data residency commitments, or revenue share must be escalated to Legal and Finance Director. For highly restricted customer requirements (e.g., on-prem data handling), route to Private Deployments PM and Security.

4. Record keeping
   - All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to Contract Repository and linked to the associated opportunity in CRM within 3 business days. Extract key dates (effective, term, renewal, termination) into the Contract register.

Revenue recognition & billing policy (summary)

Principles: Apply ASC 606: identify contract(s) with customer, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize revenue when/over time as obligations are satisfied.

1. Revenue types & typical treatment
   - Subscription (hosted API, dedicated plans): Recognize over the coverage period ratably (deferred revenue).
   - Usage-based (per-token, embeddings): Recognize as usage occurs; bill monthly in arrears unless prepay is used.
   - One-time professional services: Recognize over time when customer receives and benefits (percentage of completion) or at point-in-time if criteria met.
   - Hardware sales (Private on-prem appliances): Typically recognized at point of transfer of control; assess for separation of hardware vs. managed services.

2. Billing cadence & invoicing
   - Standard billing cycle: Monthly in arrears for usage; monthly or quarterly for subscription as contracted.
   - Prepaid arrangements: Record as deferred revenue and amortize over coverage.
   - Invoicing process: Ops prepares invoice in billing system, Finance reviews for completeness, then sends to customer with payment terms.

3. Discounts, credits & refunds
   - Commercial discounts must be encoded on the contract. Service credits for SLA breaches are capped at the contractually defined amount and accounted for as reductions to revenue. Refunds require VP-level approval and finance accounting notes.

4. Accounting close controls
   - Month-end close checklist includes deferred revenue roll-forward, unbilled revenue reconciling items, and revenue cut-off tests. All revenue journal entries require supporting contract reference and approval by Finance Manager.

Templates & artifacts (location)

- Budget template: Finance Drive / Budgeting / BudgetTemplate_2033.xlsx
- Procurement portal: procurement.redwood.internal
- Contract library & templates: /confluence/legal/contract-templates
- Revenue policy detailed guidance: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/revenue-recognition-billing-policy-2026.json

Key controls & KPIs

- Forecast accuracy target: +/- 3% for next 90 days, +/- 5% for 12-month ARR.
- Purchase order compliance: >= 98% of non-emergency spend on PO.
- Contract upload timeliness: 100% within 3 business days.
- Deferred revenue reconciliation exceptions: 0 critical items at month-end.

Change management and exceptions

- Policy changes are approved by Finance Director and Legal partner and communicated to stakeholders.
- Exceptions must be documented with business rationale, owner, and mitigation; Finance maintains an exceptions register.

Appendices

A. Approval matrix (summary)
| Item | Approver | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| <= $25k spend | BU Lead | Auto-approval in portal |
| $25k–$250k | Procurement + Finance | One-off vendor review |
| > $250k | Exec sponsor + Finance Dir | Multi-year requires Legal & CFO |

B. Common GL codes (sample)
- 5100: Cloud Infrastructure Expense
- 5200: Third-party SaaS
- 6100: Capitalized Hardware
- 7000: Revenue - Hosted API

C. Quick checklist for new customer contracts
1. Confirm customer legal entity and billing details.
2. Ensure SOW clearly lists deliverables, acceptance criteria, and pricing cadence.
3. Identify revenue impact (upfront vs. recurring) and notify RevRec lead.
4. Upload executed contract to repository and link to CRM.

Contact & escalation

Document maintenance

- Owner: Finance-legal team. Review cycle: annual or sooner when major accounting guidance changes occur. For tactical changes (e.g., threshold adjustments), update doc and notify all stakeholders via email and team channel.

End of playbook.
